questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between regression and classification?
options: Regression predicts a continuous number; classification predicts a category
Classification never uses numeric math internally
Regression only works with one feature
Classification cannot output probabilities
questions.explain: Regression outputs a value on a continuous scale (like price); classification outputs a discrete category (like spam/not spam), even though it's usually computed from an internal numeric score.

questions.q: In the lesson's scikit-learn comparison on the interleaved-crescents dataset, why did Linear SVM score lower (0.88) than RBF SVM (0.97)?
options: Linear SVM used less training data
Linear SVM can only draw a straight decision boundary, which can't cleanly separate two interleaved crescent shapes
RBF SVM doesn't use a decision boundary at all
The two models were evaluated on different datasets
questions.explain: A straight line genuinely cannot separate two interleaved crescent shapes well, while RBF SVM can curve its boundary to match the shape of the data, scoring higher as a result.

options: The maximum number of classes a model can predict
The line or curve separating the regions a classifier assigns to different classes
The point where training stops
A synonym for the loss function
questions.explain: A decision boundary is where a classifier's internal score crosses its threshold — everywhere on one side gets one predicted class, everywhere on the other side gets another.

questions.q: What does `predict_proba` give you that a hard class label alone does not?
options: The model's training time
A probability per class, so you can distinguish a barely-confident prediction from a highly confident one
The decision boundary's exact equation
A list of all features used
questions.explain: A hard label collapses everything to a single class with no sense of confidence. predict_proba exposes the underlying probability per class, so a 51%-confident prediction can be treated differently than a 99%-confident one even though both yield the same hard label.

questions.q: Classifying a handwritten digit as one of 0 through 9 is an example of what kind of classification?
options: Binary classification
Regression
Multi-class classification
Unsupervised clustering
questions.explain: With ten possible output categories (digits 0-9), this is multi-class classification, as opposed to binary classification's two categories.
